title: Understanding the decay of proteins: A method to study time dependent response of pM concentration of insulin at microwave frequencies
author: Verma, Daya

steps.title: Prepare insulin stock solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve human recombinant insulin (Sigma Aldrich) to a concentration of 10 mg ml⁻¹ in 25 mM HEPES buffer (Sigma Aldrich); keep the solution at a concentration >1 mg ml⁻¹ for storage.

steps.title: Make pM insulin test solutions
steps.instruction: Dilute the 10 mg ml⁻¹ insulin stock with 25 mM HEPES buffer to obtain insulin concentrations ranging from 35 pM to 378.78 pM, the range found in human blood.

steps.title: Cool and monitor samples
steps.instruction: Store the prepared insulin solutions at 5 °C and continuously monitor the temperature with a digital probe‑type thermometer.

steps.title: Assemble composite dielectric resonator
steps.instruction: Mount a c‑axis oriented single‑crystal sapphire puck (dielectric constant 11.5, height 8 mm, diameter 20 mm) together with a polycarbonate sample‑holding disk (SHD) of thickness 1 mm, diameter 20 mm, having a ring cavity 0.5 mm wide and 0.5 mm deep near the rim.

steps.title: Connect network analyser
steps.instruction: Connect the assembled resonator to a Rohde & Schwarz ZVA 50 vector network analyser; verify that the sapphire resonator alone resonates at 17.59 GHz with Q = 86 122 (room temperature, WGE800 mode) and the composite resonator at 17.5485 GHz with Q = 17 000. Record loss tangents: sapphire 3.6 × 10⁻⁶, SHD 0.00708.

steps.title: Load sample into SHD ring
steps.instruction: Using a micropipette, manually dispense one of the following volumes of insulin solution—0.2 µL, 0.4 µL, 0.8 µL, 1.2 µL, or 1.6 µL—into the 0.5 mm ring cavity of the SHD, ensuring the liquid fully occupies the cavity without air bubbles.

steps.title: Measure dielectric response
steps.instruction: With the network analyser set to the WGE800 mode (~17 GHz), record the permittivity and dielectric relaxation time of the loaded sample; the total time for changing the sample and acquiring the observation is 15 s.
